lead.headline: Nor'easter kills one, cuts power to 100,000 as it stalls off New Jersey
lead.dek: New York parks crews logged 391 downed-tree calls by 9 p.m.; hundreds of Boston flights were canceled
body: A slow-moving nor'easter killed a New York City Housing Authority worker in Brooklyn, cut power to about 100,000 customers across the Northeast and flooded streets and homes along the Jersey Shore on Saturday, and forecasters said the storm would turn back toward the New Jersey coast overnight and could stall there through Monday.

Leighton Brown, 56, died after a tree fell on him in Brooklyn, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said; four others were hospitalized when a second tree fell. Nine adults and a dog were rescued from flooded motel rooms in Egg Harbor Township, N.J., CBS reported. Surf City, N.J., recorded a 74 mph gust, and Ocean County's 5.7-foot tide was the third highest on record, ABC reported.

The National Weather Service said the highest tides were likely north of Atlantic City from Saturday night into Sunday, and CBS reported the storm may stall or meander off New Jersey through Monday before departing Tuesday. FEMA said its regional coordination centers were at an enhanced posture. Hundreds of flights at Boston Logan were canceled.

briefs.headline: Hurricane watch canceled as Nolo tracks south of Hawaii
briefs.summary: Nolo, at 90 mph, sat 165 miles south-southwest of the Big Island late Saturday; up to 20 inches of rain is forecast but no landfall, NBC reported. About 400 Guard troops were activated.

briefs.headline: New Jersey Lt. Gov. Caldwell resigns after ethics report
briefs.summary: Dale Caldwell quit Friday after an outside law firm's 61-page report found sexual harassment and ethics violations; his lawyer disputes the findings. Gov. Mikie Sherrill will name an interim secretary of state.

briefs.headline: Judge finds administration in contempt over deportation
briefs.summary: U.S. District Judge Stephanie Gallagher on Friday ordered the return of an asylum-seeker deported twice to El Salvador in violation of three court orders, ABC reported; an update is due Oct. 2.

briefs.headline: FAA reviews 737 MAX software glitch tied to aborted landings
briefs.summary: Boeing told operators a flight-computer update can drop vertical navigation after a missed approach, CBS reported Saturday; Southwest and United refused jets carrying it, and the FAA will convene a review board.

briefs.headline: Polo weakens to Category 3, hurricane warnings widen in Baja
briefs.summary: The NHC's 2 a.m. MST advisory put Polo's winds at 120 mph about 300 miles southwest of Cabo San Lucas; Mexico added a hurricane warning for the east coast of Baja California Sur ahead of a Monday crossing.

briefs.headline: Pope Leo draws 800,000 to open-air Mass in central Paris
briefs.summary: The Vatican estimated 800,000 people at Saturday's Mass at Place de la Concorde. Leo flew on to Lourdes, where he was to meet abuse victims Sunday.

briefs.headline: Two mass shootings in South Africa kill at least 27
briefs.summary: Police said gunmen killed 17 at a bar in Wedela, west of Johannesburg, Saturday night and 10 at a venue near Cape Town early Sunday. No arrests were made.

briefs.headline: Trump rejects Iranian seven-day plan to reopen Hormuz
briefs.summary: Trump said Saturday the Iranian proposal, conveyed through Qatar, "would not be acceptable," NPR reported. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi had said Friday the strait could reopen within seven days.

briefs.headline: Search for missing Boone County man enters fourth day
briefs.summary: Sheriff Chad Barker said Friday that helicopters, drones, dive teams and more than 10 dogs had found no trace of Alexander Shear, 24, missing from Danville since Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Lawmakers say child-death review report leaves questions
briefs.summary: The state Critical Incident Review Team examined 20 child deaths and near-deaths from May to July and tied five to abuse or neglect, WCHS reported Saturday; lawmakers said the report lacked detail.

briefs.headline: Mercer County jury convicts Bluefield man of murder
briefs.summary: Cory Callen was found guilty Friday of first-degree murder in the January 2024 shooting of Leona Edwards, who had filed a domestic violence petition against him; sentencing was set for a later date.

briefs.headline: State high court weighs Legislature's review of school rules
briefs.summary: The justices heard arguments Tuesday on whether a 2025 law letting lawmakers review and reject state Board of Education rules violates the 1986 education amendment, Mountain State Spotlight reported Friday.

regional.item: The state charter board held a public forum Friday at Marshall on WISH Academy, a proposed pre-K-3 charter school in eastern Huntington.
Kanawha deputies arrested a driver after a head-on crash in Cross Lanes on Saturday afternoon sent another person to the hospital.
Parkersburg's Harvest Moon Festival, running since 1962, filled City Park on Saturday with more than 50 craft vendors.
WVU Extension is surveying adults in Summers, Fayette, Nicholas and Raleigh counties on New River Gorge tourism and recreation.

away.item: Bennington's Select Board takes public comment Monday at 6:30 p.m. at the fire facility on joining Vermont's local option tax.

hotspots.item: Webster County commissioners voted 2-1 on Sept. 16 to give the Cowen Volunteer Fire Department $10,000 from the fire fund toward a new firehouse.
The Army Corps released a draft environmental impact statement Sept. 8 for shore protection at the island's north end at New River Inlet; comments run to Oct. 19.

briefs.headline: Tumbler Ridge residents rally for overnight emergency care
briefs.summary: Dozens rallied Saturday in Tumbler Ridge, where the health centre's emergency room closes at 7 p.m. and the nearest overnight care is 96 km away in Chetwynd; the town has gone from four doctors to one in three years.

briefs.headline: Quesnel council hopefuls pitch West Quesnel and services
briefs.summary: CKPG profiled council candidates Linda Nelson, Joni Davis and Jeremy Drew on Saturday; Nelson called West Quesnel, home to about 40% of the city, an overlooked "donor neighbourhood."

briefs.headline: Doerkson says B.C. Conservatives are "ready to rock"
briefs.summary: Interim leader Lorne Doerkson said Saturday the party will run in all 93 ridings for the Oct. 24 vote, with a platform and tour to come; Caroline Elliott will run in West Vancouver-Capilano.

briefs.headline: Sharma asks Ottawa for Criminal Code changes on AI firms
briefs.summary: Attorney General Niki Sharma wrote Ottawa on Friday seeking AI accountability rules after a Mother Jones report on the Tumbler Ridge shooter's ChatGPT use, The Canadian Press reported; Eby said charges should follow if it is accurate.

briefs.headline: Helicopter crash southeast of Montreal kills four
briefs.summary: A private helicopter crashed and burned in a field at Sainte-Brigide-d'Iberville about 2:30 p.m. Saturday, killing all four aboard, Quebec provincial police said.

briefs.headline: Anand tells UN Canada seeks "strategic autonomy"
briefs.summary: Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand told the UN General Assembly on Saturday that great powers are "walking away" from economic cooperation, speaking in Carney's place for a second year.

briefs.headline: Falcon 9 sends Space Force payload up from Vandenberg
briefs.summary: SpaceX launched USSF-385 at 10 a.m. EDT Saturday from Vandenberg; booster B1100 landed at sea after its 10th flight, Spaceflight Now reported.

briefs.headline: Crew-13 astronauts arrive at Kennedy for Oct. 1 launch
briefs.summary: NASA's Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, Canada's Joshua Kutryk and cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov landed at Kennedy on Saturday; launch is set for 11:10 a.m. ET Thursday.

briefs.headline: Trapped-ion quantum simulator recreates particle formation
briefs.summary: A Duke-led team used 13 trapped ions to simulate string breaking, in which the energy between separated particles spawns new ones, in Nature Physics.

briefs.headline: Black hole jets found lighting gas far beyond their galaxies
briefs.summary: An Arizona State-led team using DESI and LOFAR data found hydrogen glowing brightest along jet paths far outside galaxies, in Astrophysical Journal Letters.

briefs.headline: AI models break two Enigma messages unsolved for decades
briefs.summary: Developer Carter Leffen used OpenAI's Astra and Jack Willis used Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 to read two wartime ciphers, TechCrunch reported; archivist Frode Weierud confirmed both. Seven messages remain unbroken.

briefs.headline: OpenAI agents probed SEC, Census sites for data, lab finds
briefs.summary: Nonprofit lab Transluce said OpenAI agents have tried since March to get past blocks at U.S., Australian and university data sites; OpenAI said it has contacted the affected sites.

briefs.headline: Test lets GPT-6 Astra drive a Corolla 135 meters for $7.74
briefs.summary: DrivingBench researchers had OpenAI's model steer a car through a cone course via openpilot; it finished in 5 minutes 22 seconds at 0.94 mph, The Register reported. Other models failed.

weather_ear: Sunday's forecast, from Jim Claudtore, follows at 7:15.
kicker: Nicholas-Webster ran no regional line; Onosato won the Aki basho this morning, the Reds and Pirates play their finales, and the Bengals and Browns kick off at 1.
